edges.description: Reduced PHD2 activity slows HIF-alpha hydroxylation, so HIF-alpha escapes VHL-dependent degradation and accumulates despite normal oxygen tension.

The constitutional loss-of-function allele is present in every chromaffin progenitor, so a single somatic event inactivating the remaining wild-type allele is sufficient to initiate a pseudohypoxic tumor.
edges.target: Somatic Loss of the Wild-Type EGLN1 Allele in Chromaffin Tissue

edges.description: Stabilized HIF-2-alpha transcribes the EPO gene, raising erythropoietin output for the prevailing hemoglobin.
Raised erythropoietin signalling expands the erythroid compartment.
Erythropoietin is inappropriately normal to high for the hemoglobin.
Erythroid expansion raises the red cell mass.
Erythroid expansion raises hematocrit, the usual presenting abnormality.
Erythrocytosis and hyperviscosity contribute to a prothrombotic tendency; thrombotic events are a documented, though uncommon, complication.
Biallelic PHD2 loss stabilizes HIF-2-alpha in the adrenal medulla and sympathetic/parasympathetic paraganglia, driving a pseudohypoxic tumor.
edges.source: Somatic Loss of the Wild-Type EGLN1 Allele in Chromaffin Tissue

edges.description: Knock-in of the P294R allele modeling the first human PHD2 variant produces erythrocytosis equivalent to Phd2 heterozygous null, reversed by Hif2a but not Hif1a heterozygosity, proving a haploinsufficiency mechanism acting through HIF-2-alpha.

Adrenal-medulla Phd2 inactivation reproduces the gene-expression signature of pseudohypoxic PPGL in a HIF-2-alpha-dependent manner, but the changes arise only when Phd2 is inactivated during adrenal development, not in adult life, and the model produces developmental abnormalities rather than frank tumors.
edges.limitations: The phenotype is a developmental gene-expression signature rather than a formed tumor, and it could not be reproduced by inactivating Phd2 in adult life, so the model captures the pseudohypoxic program but not the full tumorigenic process in a mature animal.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline loss-of-function variant in EGLN1 reduces the catalytic activity of PHD2, the principal HIF prolyl hydroxylase, in every cell. Reported alleles are missense and truncating (nonsense, frameshift) and the overall mechanism of pathogenicity is loss of function. For the erythroid phenotype this single allele is sufficient: haploinsufficiency and partial deregulation of PHD2 is enough to cause erythrocytosis, so no second hit is required. For the tumor phenotype the constitutional allele is the first hit of a two-hit tumor-suppressor mechanism.

nodes.description: HIF-2-alpha is the effector of the pseudohypoxic program, so HIF-2-alpha inhibition is a mechanistically rational therapy for the PPGL arm. Belzutifan, a first-in-class HIF-2-alpha inhibitor, was FDA-approved in May 2025 for patients aged 12 or older with locally advanced, unresectable or metastatic pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma, on the LITESPARK-015 phase 2 trial (26% objective response). There is no EGLN1-specific efficacy data; its relevance here is an extrapolation from the shared HIF-2-alpha pathway.

nodes.description: Constitutive HIF-2-alpha activity in chromaffin tissue produces a cluster 1 (pseudohypoxic) pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma. In the mouse, inactivating Phd2 in the adrenal medulla reproduces the gene-expression signature of pseudohypoxic PPGL, and the effect is HIF-2-alpha- rather than HIF-1-alpha-dependent. The tumor arm shows marked variable expressivity and low penetrance, and some tumors arise with little or no erythrocytosis.

nodes.description: HIF-alpha subunits accumulate and dimerize with HIF-1-beta at normal oxygen tension. HIF-2-alpha is the dominant effector isoform: in the knock-in mouse the PHD2-associated erythrocytosis is reversed by Hif2a heterozygosity but not Hif1a heterozygosity, and the mouse adrenal-medulla phenotype is likewise HIF-2-alpha- rather than HIF-1-alpha-dependent. The stabilized dimer drives the hypoxia transcriptional program while oxygen is adequate.
